WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.title: Warp Train
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_1.descriptio:
A flash of white light erupts. When you open your eyes again, you seem to have arrived in a place filled with advanced technology.
Strangely, beyond the window is pure darkness, and you cannot sense your current state of motion at all. Yet somehow, you feel you are inside a [blue][jitter]moving train[/jitter][/blue] carriage.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_1.options.SK: Jump straight to the fight/escape choice.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_2.descriptio: You cautiously explore this unfamiliar place, opening one train door after another, only to see the exact same scene every time. Are you going to be trapped in this cursed place forever?! You try to stay calm, but your pace grows faster and faster, betraying the fear swelling inside you...
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_3.descriptio: [green]???[/green]: Stuffing these self-harmers back into their den is already easy, Tommy.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_4.descriptio:
[green]???[/green]: Stuffing these self-harmers back into their den is already easy, Tommy.
[red]???[/red]: Yeah, the Doctor was right. Our love for each other gave us strength.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_5.descriptio:
[green]???[/green]: Stuffing these self-harmers back into their den is already easy, Tommy.
[red]???[/red]: Yeah, the Doctor was right. Our love for each other gave us strength.
[green]???[/green]: No matter how many times we grind these disgusting pests to dust, they still crawl back out.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_6.descriptio:
[green]???[/green]: Stuffing these self-harmers back into their den is already easy, Tommy.
[red]???[/red]: Yeah, the Doctor was right. Our love for each other gave us strength.
[green]???[/green]: No matter how many times we grind these disgusting pests to dust, they still crawl back out.
[red]???[/red]: Still, this should keep them quiet for a while.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_7.descriptio:
Suddenly, you hear [red]voices[/red] [gold]ahead[/gold]. You realize this may be your [jitter][blue]only way out[/blue][/jitter] of this damned place. Whether what lies ahead is [green]good[/green] or [red]bad[/red], you must [rainbow]go find out[/rainbow]————
(Note: This event contains mild [red]gore[/red] and [red][sine]horror elements[/sine][/red]. If this may cause discomfort, you can [blue]leave now[/blue]!)
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_7_LEAVE.desc: You choose to leave and exit this bizarre train event.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_8.descriptio: Following the source of the voices, you arrive at a [sine][gold]strange[/gold][/sine] town.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_9.descriptio:
???: Mr. Tommy and Miss Mary are the great heroes of our town!!
???: Tommy!! Mary!!! Incredible!!!!
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_10.descripti:
The bloody scene before you shocks you to your core... your stomach churns, and you can barely hold it in anymore!
"Urgh!..."
You make such a loud noise that the people inside cannot miss it.
"Who is it!? An intruder... from another carriage!"
"Kill him!"
"Kill him!"
"I will fold him into a triangle, then Mommy will definitely reward me!"
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_10.options.E: Escape. Heal [blue]{Heal}[/blue] HP and add [red]Injury[/red] to your deck.
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_11.descripti:
Terrified, you turn and run. You [jitter][red]frantically[/red][/jitter] shove open carriage door after carriage door and sprint in the opposite direction. After who knows how long, you black out again...
When you open your eyes, you have escaped the train and returned to the familiar Spire.
Was it all just a dream? You shake your head and force yourself not to think too much about it, never noticing the [sine]several vivid [red]scars[/red] that somehow appeared on your arm...[/sine]
WARP_TRAIN_EVENT.pages.PAGE_12.descripti: You barely survive this nightmare. The roar of the train fades into the distance, but the memory still lingers in your mind.
SINGING_MACHINE_EVENT.title: Singing Machine
SINGING_MACHINE_EVENT.pages.INITIAL.desc:
A melody made from a living person is the most beautiful of all!!!
From the outside, it looks like nothing more than an ordinary industrial meat grinder. Yet rumors say the machine has a strange power: when you approach—or even touch it—people cannot help but leap inside. Then the lid shuts and it begins to "operate." Generally, one "operation" lasts about 5 minutes.
After several experiments, we reached one conclusion: it wants to create a kind of "music" through its "operation."
SINGING_MACHINE_EVENT.pages.APPROACH_FOL: "I-I-I... I know... this s-s-sounds... crazy, b-b-but! But... heehee, I-I-I have to... hear that m-m-melody again! My b-brain... my head is f-f-full of... those things!!! Hehehe... to hear that melody... I've tried so, so... so many... attempts!"
SINGING_MACHINE_EVENT.pages.OBSERVE_FOLL: "████ leaned in and stared at the machine, while I only wanted to finish the observation report and leave that eerie place. It seems we couldn't agree. He said they all have their own special abilities, but I didn't care. I warned ████ not to get any closer, yet ████ took another step forward..."
FUNERAL_OF_THE_DEAD_BUTTERFLIES_EVENT.pa:
A mourner bearing a heavy burden came here to redeem all beings.

But now, like everyone else, it is trapped here, wandering in despair with its edge dulled, left only with hollow faith.

It delivers coffins for those who have nowhere to go, though this coffin is far from enough to lay those innocent scapegoats to rest.
Choose [blue]{PickCount}[/blue] from [blue]{ChoiceCount}[/blue] random upgraded cards and add it to your deck.
(Requires the Book of Dead Butterflies relic. In multiplayer, all players must have it.)
(Requires the Book of Dead Butterflies relic. In multiplayer, all players must have it.)
You open the old book. Butterfly dust settles on your fingers, taking away memories that were useless but heavy. When the cover closes, you feel lighter, and colder.
A white butterfly rests in your palm and becomes a clean page. It is not warm, but it records a technique that was already waiting for you.
After the gunshots fade, the butterflies return to silence. The old book is replaced by a new page, as if the funeral has finally ended.

XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.INITIAL.o: Choose [blue]1[/blue] of [blue]3[/blue] [gold]E.G.O pages[/gold] belonging to Xiao and add it to your deck.

XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.RESONATED: Xiao's embers resonate with you. You take the chosen E.G.O page into your deck and leave.
The reception is over. Xiao's embers fade, and silence returns to the Library.
KALI_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.title: Reception — The Red Mist
“That great crimson blade was a prototype E.G.O extracted by chance.”
“That armor is an E.G.O manifested by Kali herself, unique to the Red Mist.”
“By now, you should know that not every E.G.O possesses that kind of power.”
“Rather, very few people can draw out the power of E.G.O the way Kali did…”

SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.locked.title: Not Yet Available
SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.locked.description: Receiving a guest with a specified Librarian is not yet available.
SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.ESCAPED.descri: You avoid the special guest and continue onward.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.1: You have all died. No one remains by my side.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.2: In here, you fought with me till the end… and perished.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.3: I feel lonely as a dragon soaring in the air, my heart heavy with regret.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.5: I only see darkness. I can’t see a step ahead.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.6: Where must I go? Where does the courage to put one’s foot forward come from?
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.7: What did you believe in so firmly until your last moments?
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.8: Was it the hope that we will emerge victorious… a strong leader… or the goal of earning the books…?
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.9: I sadly won’t be able to hear your answers now.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.10: However, as the breath of life momentarily rests inside us before it scatters to return to its source… I will meet you again one day; and I may ask you my question then.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.12: You again. You’re one persistent conversationalist, are you not.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.13: …I won’t collapse or succumb to fear out of the despair I brought onto myself.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.14: There’s nothing that a human… that I cannot overcome.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.15: I believe that I will reach the ideal consequence if I remain steadfast and proceed with perseverance… I sincerely, ingenuously believe this.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.16: …No. There’s no need to be disheartened in the face of such a thing. Without despair, hope won’t be needed either.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.17: Fear is born for there is hope, but bravery is born because there is fear…
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.18: Without all these, there is no life. And what is life without a reason to live…
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.19: So why would I not bask in this sensation of vitality?
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.20: I will still fight for my own sake.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.21: Not to disregard the colleagues who gave their lives for me.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.22: …No. Rather, I would be disregarding their sacrifice if I gave up here because of what happened to them.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.24: I don’t see myself ever agreeing with your words.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_ONE.25: A lone tree cannot form a forest on its own, you say… An interesting tale.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_TWO.0: Even if I am alone, night will come.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_TWO.1: And every night is followed by dawn…
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_TWO.2: A mere star that will fade cannot hope to best the light of the rising sun.
XIAO_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY_TWO.3: Be prepared; for today, a Star of the City shall be gone.

RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.TOOK_D: You accept the Will of the Prescript and abandon the reception.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.FLED_W: Your wounds close, but you flee carrying a guilt that will not fade.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.COMPLE:
Risking one's life to fabricate Prescripts… solely to prove that one's will was free…
Yet those actions were also part of the Prescript… part of the City's will…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.1: Fourteen steps to the right… Twenty-three steps to the left…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.3: How… far down does this go…?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.5: The sound, it’s getting louder… And I see a dim light…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.6: …Is it really okay to head inside?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.8: I guess I have no choice.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.9: …What’s this…? What are these huge machinations supposed to be…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.10: Welcome~ Welcome~! It must’ve been an exhausting journey here, come on in and make yourself at home~!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.13: It’s so nice to see a guest after such a long time. Come on, now! Don’t be shy and step right in!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.16: You were invited by the Prescript, right…?!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.18: The likes of you couldn’t even dream of finding this place without the guidance of the Prescript!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.19: It only invites people here on a very extraordinary occasion, so consider yourself honored~!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.20: …Does this place have something to do with the Prescripts?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.21: Yes-oh-yes, it has plenty to do with them. This is the birthplace of Prescripts.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.23: Your face tells me that you must have a lot you’d like to hear!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.24: And that’s good! I was really bored, too, actually… You should take a seat first, here. This will be a loooong story! Here’s your chair…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.25: Sorry I have no tea. It’s hard to come by warm water down here… Oh, where are my manners. What’s your name? Are you a Proxy? Or a Messenger? My name’s Moirai!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.26: H-hold on. Could you please slow down…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.27: First off, I’m Yan… Yan Vismok… I’m a Messenger. I only started working less than a month ago…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.28: Yan! So you were a Messenger.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.29: Yes… I’ve been delivering Prescripts full of absurd and brutal orders.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.30: Oh, I understand. Prescripts are cruel indeed. And knotty, too, which gets some people killed.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.31: …I had to hear many resentful remarks and screams from the people who received their Prescripts.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.32: Are you… Are you the one who wrote those ridiculous Prescripts?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.33: Yeesh, so scary! Don’t scowl at me so dreadfully, now.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.35: No, I’m not responsible for the contents of the Prescripts. My occupation is to manage these spinning wheels and loom.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.40: Can you hear this sound? Can you feel the tremor, climbing up your feet and touching your bosom?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.41: …I can feel a tiny quake, yes. But… what about it? It’s just a small vibration.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.42: Wrong! This isn’t a simple tremor.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.43: You’re feeling the heartbeat of the City.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.45: Those vibrations move this pendulum over here… and I spin the wheels to make threads.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.47: Oh, why hear me describe it when you can see it in action? Here, why don’t you come closer and take a look~ A new Prescript is about to be born!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.48: The pendulum swings above the threads I spin, inscribing meaning on them.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.49: …Meaning? All I see are random patterns.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.50: It could seem hazy at first. This is the language of the City, after all. You obviously won’t recognize it, no-oh-no!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.51: The language of the City? Were there more languages left to be found…?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.52: Mmm… It’s a different kind from the languages people use. Oh, it certainly is.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.53: The thing is… I have no idea what it means, either~
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.54: But we’ll soon be able to find out.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.55: There are fifty-seven spinning wheels here.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.56: The threads spun from those wheels are then put in this loom, and I modestly weave cloth from them.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.59: And there it is! Look. A Prescript has been created~!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.61: …‘To Chae-heon. When you see a person on a three-way intersection waving their hand seven times, follow them to their house.’
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.63: Alright~ No time to be spacing out! We should send this Prescript to a Messenger for delivery, right?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.65: …Let’s see, let’s see~ The code is N… N… Next to L… N920… and 1…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.66: There it is! Pipe number N9201 is right here!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.67: Now we roll up this Prescript and put it in here. The Prescript will travel along the pipe all the way to the surface.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.69: This can’t be… Who made the spinning wheels, the loom, and the pipes, then?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.70: I have no clue~ I was led here by a Prescript, too.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.71: Oh—oh, my predecessor was waiting for me when I arrived~ But they left after receiving a Prescript one day.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.73: Not really? I don’t have much else to do, anyway.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.74: Do you have any idea how many people died because of your stupid randomly generated commands…?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.75: If this is where all Prescripts are made… Then you could’ve at least tweaked them a little so they’re not as cruel.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.76: …I’m doing this because a Prescript ordered me to create and send Prescripts down here, though.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.77: If I broke this Prescript, the Prescripts will get me killed…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.78: What are you talking about! You’re the one in charge of sending out Prescripts!
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.79: What if there’s another Weaver like me somewhere in another Nest?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.80: You don’t possibly think that I’m the only one mailing all the Prescripts for the City, do you?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.81: Someone has to be making the contents of the Prescripts, but who could it be…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.82: In my opinion, that’d be the City itself.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.83: The pendulum inscribing patterns on the threads swings according to the City’s motions, like I said just before.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.84: Footsteps of pedestrians walking around on the surface… Quakes coming from construction sites… Impacts created from some clumsy person falling on the floor… Echoes of people’s screams…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.85: Every little event happening in the City becomes a vibration that moves the pendulum.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.86: Even the sound of us talking.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.87: At the end of the day, us City folk can never be free from the City.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.88: Every deed committed by denizens of the City is ultimately the City’s deed. We’re representing its will in a sense.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.89: All the cruel things we’ve been committing were out of the City’s volition?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.90: Why did the City… have to be that way?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.92: The City was built by people, and their cruel nature had to naturally reflect on their creation.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.94: This is a mess… People built the City… and now the City is controlling the people…?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.95: Does the order really matter much? I think the point is this! That whatever we do, we’re essentially part of the City.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.96: All you do is weave cloth in this peaceful bunker… You probably have no idea what kind of brutal outcomes that piece of cloth you make can bring.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.97: That’s why you can talk about this with such a carefree attitude…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.98: You’re right, that’s beyond me. I only do what I was ordered to do.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.99: Do I really have to care about that, though?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.100: According to the City’s will, its volition… The City’s will matches the will of the people living in it.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.102: There are beings born out of the City folk’s wants.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.103: Humans want to walk the path that’s given to them. They’re afraid to face the consequences of their actions and take responsibility for them.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.104: They know that they will only end up going the wrong way if they try to make their own decisions.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.105: They’d rather rely on something and expect things from it rather than to live a life of struggle.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.106: People without purpose in their lives desiring and yearning for something to open up a way for them…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.107: It could be someone wishing for equality amidst the savagery and voyeurism…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.108: Or it could be the vain hopes of those who want the City to thrive forevermore, providing for all of its inhabitants…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.109: That’s how gods were born; people needed them.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.110: They didn’t pop into existence because someone told them to. They can’t be made up by anyone, nor can they be oppressed.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.111: You can’t blame anyone for this.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.112: So many people, so many residents of the City want them…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.113: Thus, they’re the fear that will draw near them, the temptation of happiness… The promises and wishes of all people.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.114: Are you starting to get… why the Prescripts came into existence?
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.118: People weren’t doing inhumane things because I delivered Prescripts to them…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.119: Those horrible things were meant to happen anyway.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.121: You’re right, I think I see it now.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.122: It’s the City… It’s because people have always been cruel. Humans are born that way… And they have desperate wishes.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.123: It doesn’t matter if they were pure wishes welled up from innocent hearts or ambitions born from greed, this is the result of what everyone wished for.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.124: Killing people with my own hands, or taking away invaluable things from others…
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.125: Shuddering in guilt listening to those horrid screams, while I tried my best to seem unfazed.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.126: They were all useless feelings eating away at my heart.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.127: …Exactly. I’m just a tiny part of the world, I can never change the wishes of all people… There’s no way I can defy this flow.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.128: What I did was part of the City… The will of the City.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.129: Forging Prescripts out of spite and delivering them could be traced to the City’s volition, not my free will.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.130: But that equates to my volition in the end.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.131: The City and I… and every person in this City were one and the same.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.133: …Moirai. The City must know where I should go next.
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.136: …Oh, don’t you worry. Just a moment, please~
RNFMABJ_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.137: …Alright, here. It’s an invitation to the Library. Prepared just for you.

IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_EVENT.pages.ENCHANTED: Iori leaves behind a violet rift in constant flux. You bind its power to an Attack.
The Purple Tear… the name of a Color. Her power was formidable as well.
The ability to cross dimensions…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.0: Why, you managed to up the ante pretty quickly, kid in Blue?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.1: It’s all thanks to your advice, my dear mentor.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.2: Without your help, I couldn’t have come this far or joined hands with this wonderful crew of allies.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.3: Come on, you’re flattering me. You’re not the type to say such things.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.4: Wouldn’t you like to join us?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.5: Sorry, but I’m just not cut out for music.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.6: That’s a pity. I’d really love to return the favor somehow.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.7: You were the only one who showed me the light when I was lost, dear mentor.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.8: Honestly, I thought you were little more than some deranged maniac until you came to me.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.9: My, you’ve got no breaks on your mouth.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.10: So, how are things going for you?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.11: The Puppeteer, Blood-red Night, L’heure du Loup, Yesterday’s Promise, the leader of the Church of Gears, the 8 o’Clock Circus, The Musicians of Bremen, The Crying Children, and one of the Eight Chefs…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.12: I’ve gathered the members so sweetly.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.13: And we’ve nourished the Library just as you advised.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.14: You were so quick about it, it’s almost obese at this point.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.16: I can finally be myself soon enough…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.17: I was lonely, to tell you the truth. So painfully lonely.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.18: The loneliness born from the belief that we could never understand each other.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.19: The two of you suffered terrible things at such a young age, so the bond between you both must’ve been even more special.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.20: You’re right. I had thought the only reason I lived was because my sister was alive…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.22: But even after Angelica left me…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.23: I was terribly lonely, yet I wanted to live.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.24: I just couldn’t give up my life with my own hands by any means.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.25: Then I had a realization: I was just suspending the inevitable.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.26: That I had merely put the meaning of my life on Angelica and run from it.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.27: The performance that will soon echo through the City will be my journey to seek the meaning to live… and be the proof of my life.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.28: All of us will be freed from loneliness.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.29: It’s a farewell to this gloomy and solitary City.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.30: Like the Pianist, all of us can become one and perform together.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.32: A dirge for Angelica… Yes. You said the power of the Distortion would be needed if I wanted to spread the beautiful melody Angelica showed me through every corner of the City.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.33: Thanks to that advice, I managed to form a wonderful crew.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.34: Take a look at the members of the ensemble, dear mentor. They can’t be compared to the humans corroded by the City.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.35: They were abandoned, scorned… struggled in anguish and sorrow after what they cherished was taken from them…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.36: But they didn’t give up; they clawed their way out of the deep dark abyss, and found their truest forms…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.37: True strength can only be pulled out of filthy, fathomless pits of despair… Nothing could rival such beauty, don’t you agree?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.38: With a crew like this… I’ll be able to inscribe that tune into every part of the City once again.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.39: While I get that your mind is brimming with enthusiasm… It’s not a won game yet, though, is it?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.40: You still have to take the Library’s Light in your own hands.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.41: Hahaha… Ah, you’re right. I was elated like a little child for a moment.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.42: Even though it’s still not in my grasp just yet…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.43: That light… I could almost touch it, but not quite snatch it…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.45: Iori, dear. I’m curious about why you live on.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.46: Hadn’t you lost all meaning to your life ages ago?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.47: I’m pretty sure you’re lonelier than most.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.48: Yet you still refuse to join us.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.49: That’s harsh, kid. I do have at least one reason to live, you know?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.50: I wonder if it’s true that you know everything, dear mentor.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.51: I’m grateful from the bottom of my heart for you coming to me and helping us prepare our performance.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.52: I thought you were helping me out of pity… I believed you were motivated by pure sympathy for me.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.53: But… the person in our hearts is bawling at us, telling us that it’s not true.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.55: Yes. She speaks to me in such a wondrous and clear voice, a voice I’d never ever heard in this world.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.56: Now, Iori… Could she be speaking the truth?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.57: Then, what’s the true motive behind my dear teacher’s assistance?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.58: Dunno. My guess is as good as yours.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.59: Maybe looking at you reminded me of my son…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.61: Ah, Iori… You’re such a tearjerker.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.62: Your son died more than 40 years ago…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.64: …What’s your true motive in helping me?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.65: I thought you’d always remain a dorky and naive little kid… Looks like you’ve grown smarter after making friends and stuff, huh?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.66: I just needed to give you a helping hand so I could reach a place I wanted to go.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.67: Mhm. A place you want to go, is it.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.68: Where could you be wanting to go so desperately to treat me with such kindness…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.69: You have the ability to jump between dimensions, you should be able to go anywhere and know anything with ease…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.70: Kid. This power isn’t as easily abusable as you might think.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.72: I don’t want you living any longer, Iori.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.74: You knew I was going to do this, didn’t you?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.75: What is my all-knowing mentor going to do now, I wonder…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.76: For your information, even you will have a hard time escaping the thick layer of barriers I’ve set up.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.78: That brain of yours you put to work was far inferior to my Thought Gears.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.80: How about I break ‘er arms and legs before she can think about running away.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.82: You’ve lost something precious to you… Surely you can understand us.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.84: Aha! How about a snake show drenched in strawberry juice?! The fleshy fruit will make an explosive display!
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.88: I wonder what your veins taste like…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.90: It’s no good eating them raw, sister. I’ll make a fine pasta out of her veins once you get ‘em out! Rosé sauce would go well with it. Hawhawhaw!
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.92: Leave some flesh and bones for me. My puppetry isn’t done yet…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.94: Iori… We don’t need you anymore.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.96: It might have been but a brief moment to you guys, but for me, it was a long and valuable time.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.97: Please don’t talk nonsense all of a sudden.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.98: Now, I have places to be…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.99: Sir Argalia! She has the invitation!
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.101: Iori, let me ask you one question.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.102: Angela! You have a guest waiting at the door!
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.103: …Can you sincerely not hear her mesmerizing voice?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.105: I’m starting to see why he’s been up to his crazy antics now.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.107: What’s with that face? Anything bothering you?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.108: They said they’re after the Library’s Light.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.109: That means their aim… overlaps with ours.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.110: I guess so. …Are you scared that they’d steal it from you?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.111: No. You and the other librarians are handling receptions well enough. I have much faith in you.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.112: Though, I would be lying if I said I had no fear.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.113: You can just say that you don’t trust us enough.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.115: Your attitude being one of those differences. You were full of pride when R Corp. challenged us. Heck, you were confident pretty much all the time.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.117: Most of the guests we’ve greeted so far had a vague purpose. They only sought to earn the books and get back.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.118: Not to have the books themselves, either… Most were planning to give them to their superiors, such as the leader of the Syndicate or the higher-ups of the Association. Of course, all of it was done on the premise that it’ll ultimately bring happiness to themselves.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.120: They have a clear objective. And their goal is the same thing I seek.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.121: There’s a considerable contrast between those who act in the interests of others and those who act strictly for themselves.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.122: I never had to worry about it being taken in the past, but the situation has changed now, hasn’t it?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.123: So, what I’m getting at is that they scare you because their goal is taking the thing you’re gathering, and not because they might be too strong?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.124: Yes. Now theft has become a concern of mine thanks to them.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.125: Phew~ That was a close call.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.126: Age hasn’t stopped my heart from still being so excitable.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.127: That aside, this place handles transportation pretty gently, unlike how I do it.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.129: Everyone and their mother’s heard about you and your Library by now, so let’s skip the introductions.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.130: Since you probably saw what was going on out there… You have a basic idea of how things went, yeah?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.132: Looking at the state of the Library… Guess I didn’t have to worry so much.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.133: And you seem to be making steady progress towards becoming a human, too.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.135: All thanks to the kiddo being quick to set up the stage, huh?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.136: Then why are you helping me?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.138: You ensured the steady growth of the Library in substance. Am I wrong?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.139: I just couldn’t leave the kid in Blue be.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.140: You want us to make sure that the Blue Sicko and his friends can’t get their hands on the Library’s power?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.142: And extract a book from me. It’ll be pretty helpful.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.143: I have a fair amount of info in my head.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.144: You’re asking to be killed nonchalantly… Are all Colors out of their minds?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.145: Course I’m not. I’ll fight with all my strength.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.146: If you can’t best this old woman… I’ll ruin the Library in my own way.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.147: Although I can’t completely kill you, I do have a number of ideas for breaking a being that has become quite close to human.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.148: I get what you’re saying. Why don’t you cut the nonsense and get inside now?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.149: The director of a library where countless bits of knowledge are accumulated wants to part with her past memories…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.151: Just focus on finding your book.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.152: Gee, aren’t you cold. But if that’s what the library director says, I gotta listen.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.154: May you find your book in this place.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.155: Whoops… There she goes. I wanted to hear more about the kid here.
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.156: He seemed pretty unstable back then…
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.157: Still, I guess he also played a part in helping the Library expand so much, huh?
IORI_SPECIAL_GUEST_STORY.159: All right. Let’s see how great this Library place is, shall we?
